entryReviews.verification: M remains inside face ABCD under both camera positions; rotating the representation changes neither the point nor its face membership.
M on AB and N on AD belong to the same convex face ABCD, so segment MN lies in that face.
The displayed diagonals AC and BD meet at the common in-plane center O=(3,3,0). This does not generalize to arbitrary intersecting projections.
X=(4,6,0) belongs to common edge BC of ABCD and BFGC; subsequent XP uses BFGC.
M, N, P lie on SA, SB, SC; MN, NP, PM use faces SAB, SBC, SCA and form the triangular boundary.
MNPQ uses the four lateral faces; QM in DHEA supplies the final boundary edge.
M on AA1 and N on AD both belong to DD1A1A; a face must contain both endpoints.
AEFB and CGHD are opposite parallel faces; the transferred line through P meets CG at Q.
z=0.5 gives an internal square, z=1 coincides with a supporting face, and z=1.1 is outside the unit cube.
X=(-3,0,0) is an external trace point; YP is the finite base edge of the section and X is not a section vertex.
T=(0,-4/3,0) lies on the line AB outside the finite edge, but still belongs to the base plane.
Auxiliary diagonal plane ACE contains points M on AE and N on CG; its use is distinct from a body face.
Plane KLC contains KM and LC; their trace point T is external to the solid and belongs to the base plane.
The displayed central point P belongs to diagonal AG; line MP and edge line CG are coplanar in ACE.
Intersecting KL and KM determine plane MKL; LN through L parallel to KM lies in the same plane.
O and T are base centers and M lies on OT with OM:MT=1:2; the axis supplies a valid auxiliary plane.
X=(0,9,0) is an auxiliary external trace point; the closed finite boundary is MNQP.
For 2x+3y+4z=level the specified levels 1, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5 yield respectively 3, 4, 5, 6 section vertices.
Parallel sections at z=0.5 and z=1.25 in a height-2 pyramid are at distances 1.5 and 0.75 from the apex; areas 2.25 and 0.5625 have ratio 1/4.
In the regular hexagonal prism AD=6 and the perpendicular height is 5, giving the displayed rectangular-section area 30.
AB perpendicular to AD alone does not prove perpendicularity to plane ABCD. AB perpendicular to both AD and AA1 proves perpendicularity to DD1A1A.
The weighted-plane levels 1, 4.5, 9.3 give a triangle, hexagon, empty section; 9 is the maximum over the unit cube and finite-edge parameters must lie in [0,1].
The oblique-parallelepiped section has opposite sides parallel but adjacent vectors satisfy dot(MN,MP)=12, so a rectangle is not justified.
Central symmetry sends x+y+z=0.5 to x+y+z=2.5. Both triangular sections have area 0.21650635094610965.
At x+y+z=0.99 and 1 there are 3 distinct vertices; at 1.01 there are 6. Coincident edge-intersection points at the critical level are counted once.
At height 1 the common level interval is [0.5,1.25] and level 0.7 cuts all lateral edges. At height 0.3 the bounds [0.5,0.34] are incompatible, so level 0.42 cuts only part of those edges.

findings.problem: Leaving a partial independent construction originally hid its saved progress from the map because active=false fell back to an unstarted legacy attempt.
findings.resolutionVerified: Any saved construction marks the card started; without competing legacy work, the map reads manual actions and the route resumes them. Started legacy work retains priority. The root-authored leave -> map -> reload -> resume regression passes.
Previously reported case-agreement issue no longer occurs in the reviewed conclusion.

constructionIntegrationContract.legacyEvidence: Keep task.choiceEvidence, choiceEvidenceAt and attemptEvidenceVersion unchanged. Manual actions are not task.revealed and must not upgrade old guided history.
constructionIntegrationContract.undo: Undo removes the latest accepted action and current completion while preserving help and earned historical evidence. The map may therefore show earlier verified choices while recommending continuation of the current incomplete attempt.
constructionIntegrationContract.resume: An inactive saved manual draft without competing old mode/actions/checks continues as manual. A started old guided/practice attempt keeps its previous route.
constructionIntegrationContract.laterReview: reviewDueAt includes valid historical old and manual evidence timestamps and schedules from the earliest one.
